faqs.a: 256 MiB for the entire multipart request, 2,000 files, 512 MiB extracted ZIP content, 120 seconds and two simultaneous conversions. Large HTML results download normally but preview only below 20 MiB.

faqs.q: Can it read PDFs, scanned pages or legacy .doc files?
faqs.a: No. PDF is an output format; OCR and legacy binary Word input are cut. Use DOCX, ODT, HTML, EPUB, text markup, spreadsheets or presentations supported by Pandoc.

tools.name: Typst Editor
tools.description: Write Typst documents with live preview and export them to PDF, PNG or SVG.
tools.engine_reason: The official typst binary compiles in milliseconds and needs nothing else.
tools.release_notes: Early rejections (two compiles already running, invalid paths, size limit) now read the upload first (up to the 68 MiB request cap, 10 s) and then send the JSON error, so the browser shows the message instead of 'Failed to fetch'. Runtime re-synced. Built with official Typst 0.15.1.

howto: Start it: the editor opens with an article template and its live preview.
Type: the preview recompiles 250 ms after you stop and only reloads pages that changed.
Open a folder, a zip or single files; double-click a .typ tab to make it the main file.
Click a diagnostic to jump to its file, line and column.
Export PDF (or PDF/A, PDF/UA), PNG or SVG pages, or download the whole project as a zip.

faqs.q: Does it need the internet?
faqs.a: No. The official typst 0.15.1 binary is bundled and every compile runs on your machine. The tool blocks typst package downloads.

faqs.q: Can I use @preview packages?
faqs.a: Packages already in your Typst package cache work. Others are never downloaded: copy the package files into your project and import them by path.

faqs.q: Are my files safe from the document?
faqs.a: Each compile runs in a fresh temporary folder set as the typst root, so a document cannot read files outside the project. Endless loops are killed after 60 seconds and memory is capped.

faqs.q: Is the PDF the same as running typst myself?
faqs.a: Yes. With the same flags and creation timestamp, the PDF is byte-identical to the typst CLI output (tested).

faqs.q: Can I use my own fonts?
faqs.a: Add .ttf or .otf files to the project; typst finds them. System fonts are used too unless you untick that option.

tools.name: AsciiDoc Converter
tools.description: Convert AsciiDoc documents and projects to self-contained HTML5, DocBook 5 or Markdown with Asciidoctor, offline.
tools.engine_reason: Asciidoctor.js is the official JavaScript Asciidoctor; reference comparisons match after removing the default Google Fonts import. SAFE mode confines conversion to the project. Local images, highlighting, icons and math are embedded; remote media URLs are retained with an export warning. downdoc (by Asciidoctor's lead) produces Markdown after Asciidoctor resolves includes.
tools.release_notes: Uploads drained before 403 so Connection: close clients get the JSON error.

howto: Run localtools-asciidoc-converter; the page opens at http://127.0.0.1:47132.
Paste AsciiDoc, or drop .adoc files and images, open a whole folder, or drop a zip; include:: and image:: paths keep working.
Pick the output (HTML page, HTML body, DocBook 5, Markdown) and options such as table of contents, section numbers, icons, code theme and STEM; the preview updates as you type.
Click a warning to open its file and select the line (including archive sources up to 2 MiB), then Download, Copy, or Print / PDF. Remote media warnings mean opening the export may load those URLs.
From a terminal: localtools-asciidoc-converter convert doc.adoc -o doc.html --attribute toc

faqs.q: Is the HTML the same as Asciidoctor's?
faqs.a: Yes. It is Asciidoctor.js 4.1.1 (equivalent to Asciidoctor 2.0.26); 527 HTML5 and DocBook comparisons across 267 real documents match after removing the default Google Fonts import. Local images, the default stylesheet, highlight.js colours, Font Awesome icons and math are embedded. Remote media and favicon URLs remain with a warning: opening the export may load them; the preview blocks them.

faqs.q: Can a document read files outside my project or reach the network?
faqs.a: No. Conversion runs in Asciidoctor's SAFE mode: includes, images, stylesheets and docinfo come only from the main document's folder and below, absolute and .. paths are confined to it, URI includes and remote images are never fetched, and the preview blocks all network loads.

faqs.q: How do I get a PDF?
faqs.a: asciidoctor-pdf is a Ruby tool, so it is not bundled. Use Print / PDF on the page, which prints the preview with your browser's Save as PDF.

faqs.q: What does Markdown support?
faqs.a: Markdown is produced by downdoc after Asciidoctor resolves include:: and ifdef::. It covers headings, lists, tables, admonitions, code blocks with callouts, images and links; layout-only features such as complex table spans have no Markdown equivalent.

faqs.q: What are the limits?
faqs.a: Uploads up to 64 MiB total including multipart framing, 5,000 files, zips expanding to 256 MiB, and 64 MiB of output. An exact 64 MiB pasted document exceeds the framed upload limit and returns 413. The server gives each conversion 60 s in its own process (two at a time); the CLI has no deadline. Archive diagnostic sources up to 2 MiB of encoded text can open in the editor.

tools.name: LaTeX to SVG
tools.description: Render LaTeX, MathML or AsciiMath to SVG, PNG and MathML with speech alt text, offline with MathJax.
tools.engine: MathJax 4.1.3 (TeX/MathML/AsciiMath -> SVG/MathML) + Speech Rule Engine 5 + resvg-wasm 2.6
tools.engine_reason: MathJax is the reference renderer of TeX math on the web; its lite DOM, font ranges and named entities are bundled offline. Supported equations match stock MathJax with documented standalone post-processing and Safe filtering. SRE provides optional speech; resvg rasterizes PNGs across OSes.
tools.release_notes: MathML 1 color/background attributes drawn; flat-chain time limit documented; uploads drained before 403.

howto: Run localtools-latex-to-svg; the page opens at http://127.0.0.1:47133.
Type TeX, MathML or AsciiMath; preview and copy SVG/MathML/data URI/an tag, or download SVG and PNG.
Choose display or inline style, colour and PNG scale. Tagged equations are refused: remove \tag or use align*/equation*.
Drop a .tex/.md/.txt file in Batch, or run localtools-latex-to-svg batch paper.tex -o out/ for images and manifest.json; balanced multiline document macros are supported.
Long formulas display notices when speech is omitted or glyph reuse is enabled. Downloads/copies remain complete; code preview is limited to 1 MB.
CLI/API options and limits: https://github.com/chayprabs/localtools/blob/main/latex-to-svg/USAGE.md

faqs.q: Does it need TeX or the internet?
faqs.a: No. MathJax 4 with its New Computer Modern font, the Speech Rule Engine and the resvg rasterizer are built into the program; nothing is downloaded. \require of a package that is not built in is refused.

faqs.q: Which LaTeX packages work?
faqs.a: amsmath/amssymb, mathtools, physics, mhchem, braket, cancel, color, boldsymbol, amscd, bussproofs, cases, empheq, enclose, extpfeil, gensymb, units, upgreek, textmacros, unicode and verb, plus newcommand/def/DeclareMathOperator. Balanced multiline .tex definitions are applied in batch; incomplete definitions are skipped with a notice. Tagged/numbered standalone exports are refused.

faqs.q: Is the SVG the same as MathJax in a browser?
faqs.a: The original 162-formula corpus verifies 161 supported SVGs byte for byte against stock MathJax and one explicit tagged-equation refusal; nine named MathML entities also match the stock promise API. Exports remove event handlers, external URLs and unsafe styles. Multline uses intrinsic width.

faqs.q: How are PNG sizes chosen?
faqs.a: Scale 1 is a 16 px font size; the default 4 gives 64 px, and --dpi N equals scale N/96. PNGs are limited to 64 megapixels; the background is transparent unless you pick a colour.

faqs.q: What happens with bad input?
faqs.a: Recursive macros, over 400 nesting levels and over 256 KB are refused. Each formula has a killable 10 s worker budget (30 s above 64 KB). Speech is optional: above 2048 source characters, 16384 MathML characters or 256 tree nodes it is omitted with a notice; provide alt text. Above 16384 source characters, embedded glyph reuse is enabled and reported.

tools.name: DOCX Compare
tools.description: Compare two Word documents and produce a tracked-changes redline .docx.
tools.engine_reason: WmlComparer writes genuine Word tracked changes (w:ins/w:del) at word level, including tables, footnotes and text boxes; accepting the redline gives the revised text and rejecting it gives the original (127/127 test pairs).
tools.release_notes: Multi-section documents keep sections and headers/footers; accept/reject handle tracked moves and altChunk; exact reject ranges for bookmarks ending after their paragraph; 413 for oversized uploads; no false header/footer changes; one-line CLI errors.

howto: Run localtools-docx-compare (or open DOCX Compare from your app menu); it opens in your browser.
Drop the original .docx and the revised .docx.
Set the author and date the tracked changes should carry, and tick Ignore case if letter case does not matter, then press Compare.
Read the inline preview (insertions underlined, deletions struck through) or the Changes tab, then download the redline .docx and open it in Word or LibreOffice.

To finish a reviewed document, drop it in "Accept or reject all tracked changes". From scripts: localtools-docx-compare a.docx b.docx -o redline.docx --author "Reviewer", and localtools-docx-compare accept redline.docx -o clean.docx.

faqs.q: Are these real Word tracked changes?
faqs.a: Yes. The redline contains w:ins and w:del revisions with the author and date you set, so Word and LibreOffice show them in Review and can accept or reject each one. Accepting all of them gives the revised document text; rejecting all gives the original.

faqs.q: What if a document already has tracked changes?
faqs.a: They are accepted first, so the redline shows the difference between the two documents as they currently read. The number of revisions that were accepted is shown with the result.

faqs.q: Are headers, footers, comments, formatting changes and moves shown?
faqs.a: Headers and footers are compared and their changes tracked, including image, link and field changes; unsupported header/footer layouts produce a warning. Body/note hyperlinks and bookmarks are re-anchored where possible; failure produces a warning and can drop all of them. Formatting-only changes are not marked, moved text appears as deletion plus insertion, and comments are not carried into the redline (accept/reject all keeps them). Resolving tracked moves or redlines can change empty paragraphs.

faqs.q: How big can the documents be?
faqs.a: Up to 50 MB per file. Each comparison runs in its own process with a 3-minute deadline; about 2,000 paragraphs compare in roughly 11 seconds. Zip bombs and XML entity bombs are refused.

faqs.q: Is anything uploaded?
faqs.a: No. The tool runs on 127.0.0.1 on your computer and works offline.

tools.name: Office Converter
tools.description: Convert PPTX, DOCX, XLSX and ODF documents to PDF or PNG with LibreOffice, including speaker notes.
tools.engine_reason: LibreOffice renders real DOCX/PPTX/XLSX and ODF with bundled fonts; Poppler rasterizes every PDF page. The isolated Docker image keeps this large engine consistent across hosts. Requires Landlock ABI3+ in the Linux kernel; external links/macros/active content are rejected.
tools.release_notes: Six Office/ODF formats (DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, ODT, ODP, ODS) to PDF or a ZIP of PNG pages, presentation speaker notes, local UI/CLI/API, per-job Landlock+seccomp sandbox, offline fonts.

howto: Install and start Docker using Linux containers. The Docker Linux kernel needs Landlock ABI 3+ (Linux 6.2+).
After the image is public, install Office Converter, launch it and choose one DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, ODT, ODP or ODS file up to 10 MiB.
Choose PDF or PNG pages (ZIP). For a presentation, choose slides, slides and notes, or notes only.
Convert, inspect the PDF or first PNG page, then download. The CLI and /api/convert API provide the same conversion.

faqs.q: Does this need Microsoft Office or an internet connection?
faqs.a: No. LibreOffice, Poppler and fonts are inside the image. Docker needs internet for the initial pull and updates; conversion runs offline.

faqs.q: Which documents and limits are supported?
faqs.a: DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, ODT, ODP and ODS up to 10 MiB, 100 rendered pages and 32 MiB output. PNG pages fit within 1600 pixels. Two conversions can run at once with a 90-second deadline.

faqs.q: Can I export PowerPoint speaker notes?
faqs.a: PPTX and ODP can export slides only, slides plus notes pages, or notes pages only. Both PDF and PNG output support these modes.

faqs.q: Why is a document with hyperlinks or macros rejected?
faqs.a: External links (including ordinary hyperlinks), scripts, macros, embedded executable objects, external spreadsheet formulas and encrypted documents are deliberately rejected. Remove links or active content before conversion.

faqs.q: Will the result exactly match Microsoft Office?
faqs.a: Rendering uses LibreOffice with DejaVu, Liberation and Noto fonts. Unavailable fonts are substituted, so some pagination and graphics can differ from Microsoft Office.

tools.name: EPUB Validator
tools.description: Validate EPUB files with EPUBCheck and repair common errors.
tools.engine: EPUBCheck 5.4.0 + jlink'd Temurin 21 runtime + own repair pass
tools.engine_reason: EPUBCheck is the W3C's official EPUB conformance checker; a trimmed bundled Java runtime means no Java install.
tools.release_notes: Repair: a package document with both <metadata/> and <manifest/> self-closing now gets both expanded (new manifest items land inside <manifest>). Runtime re-synced. EPUBCheck 5.4.0 on jlink'd Temurin 21.0.12.1+1 unchanged; Java sandbox policy unchanged. Java runtime source: https://github.com/adoptium/jdk21u/tree/jdk-21.0.12.1+1

howto: Start it and drop one or more .epub files onto the page.
Pick a profile (default, dictionaries, EDUPUB, indexes, previews) and the language for EPUBCheck's messages.
Press Check: messages are grouped by severity with file, line and column and a link to the EPUBCheck reference.
Press Repair to get a fixed copy: every change is listed, and the original and repaired books are both re-checked.
Download the repaired EPUB and the report as JSON or HTML.

faqs.q: Is this the real EPUBCheck?
faqs.a: Yes, the official W3C EPUBCheck 5.4.0 runs on your machine. Its messages are identical to running epubcheck.jar yourself with the same options (tested).

faqs.q: Do I need Java?
faqs.a: No. A trimmed Eclipse Temurin 21 runtime with only the modules EPUBCheck uses is bundled.

faqs.q: What does Repair change?
faqs.a: Only packaging problems that cannot change your book's content: mimetype order and compression, manifest media types and unlisted files, missing identifiers and modification dates, a missing navigation document or NCX, and stray & or HTML entities in XHTML. Everything else is flagged for a manual fix, and the original is never modified. A repair that would leave more EPUBCheck errors than the original is never kept.

faqs.q: Does anything leave my computer?
faqs.a: No. EPUBCheck runs offline under a Java security policy with no network access, so even remote DTDs or resources referenced by a book are never fetched.

faqs.q: How large can a book be?
faqs.a: Up to 256 MiB and 10,000 files per EPUB; each check is limited to 180 seconds and 1 GiB of Java heap.
